request.spec:
Show on each person their cut total: their cuts across every pool they are a member of, added
up (a pool that shows no cuts adds nothing). Show the sheet's cut total: everyone's added up.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Show on each person their cut total: their cuts across every pool they are a member of, added
up (a pool that shows no cuts adds nothing). Show the sheet's cut total: everyone's added up.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I added cut totals: each person's row shows their cut total, and the sheet shows everyone's added up. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

All the changes are in the front end. Pool cuts were already worked out in the browser from data the app already loads, so the server and stored data didn't need to change.

- **Shared calculation (`features/pools/pools.ts`):** I moved the pool-cut calculation out of the Pools screen into an exported `poolCuts()` function, so the Pools screen still shows the same cuts. A new `personCutTotals()` adds up each person's cuts across all their pools. A pool that shows no cut (an unbalanced pool, or no pot set) adds nothing. A retired member's cut is 0.
- **People screen (`features/people/people.ts`):**
  - Each row has a new "Cut total" column, `person-cut-total`.
  - Next to the other sheet totals there is a new "Cuts in total" figure, `rollup-cut-total`, which adds up every person's total, retired people included.

Each total adds up the cuts as each pool already shows them (rounded to two decimals per pool). For example, Ada's 0.51 + 0.34 gives 0.85.
